nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) was used to model brain development. It is described as a nonparametric nonlinear regression technique with additive Gaussian noise.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: A model of brain development as a function of age and sex was created by training a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model, which is a nonparametric nonlinear regression technique with additive Gaussian noise
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Holz2023.pdf.md: Method / Constructing normative models of brain structure and function

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: (1) fMRI BOLD activity (GLM regression coefficient images) during an emotional face-matching task (negative faces, positive/neutral faces, and shapes). (2) Anatomical features: nonlinear Jacobian determinants (JDs) of the deformation fields.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: normative modeling to map deviations from the typical age-related pattern at the level of the individual of (i) activity during emotion matching and (ii) of anatomical images... we decided to take the nonlinear Jacobian determinants as feature for the normative model

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex were used as predictors in the GPR model to predict brain function and structure.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: A model of brain development as a function of age and sex was created by training a Gaussian process regression (GPR) model... to predict brain function and structure
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Holz2023.pdf.md: Method / Constructing normative models of brain structure and function
